recipes.name: Lisa's Favorite Carne Asada Marinade
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon finely chopped canned chipotle pepper

steps.text: Combine orange juice, lemon juice, and lime juice for marinade in a large glass or ceramic bowl. Add cilantro, soy sauce, garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, black pepper, chipotle pepper, and oregano; stir to combine.
Slowly whisk in olive oil until well combined. Remove 1 cup of the marinade and place in a small bowl; cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for use after the steak is cooked.
Place steak between two sheets of heavy plastic (resealable freezer bags work well) on a solid, level surface. Firmly pound steak with the smooth side of a meat mallet to a thickness of 1/4 inch.
After pounding, poke steak all over with a fork. Place steak in the marinade in the large bowl, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for 24 hours.
When ready to cook, preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat, and lightly oil the grate.
Remove steak from the marinade and shake off excess. Discard the remaining marinade.
Cook steak on the preheated grill to desired doneness, about 5 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Remove steak from grill and slice across the grain.
Place on a serving platter and pour the reserved, unused marinade over top. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Lisa's Favorite Carne Asada Marinade
raw_recipe.description: This popular carne asada recipe includes a delicious spicy citrus and soy marinade to ensure the steak is juicy and tender when it comes off the grill.

video.description: Any amazing grilled taco recipe starts with the right carne asada marinade. In this video, learn how to make a tasty and versatile marinade for Mexican style beef. A long soak in a spicy citrus and soy marinade makes sure that the flank steak will be delectably tender when it comes off the grill. With its remarkable flavor and simple ingredient list, this marinade could easily become a family favorite.
video.name: How to Make the Best Carne Asada Marinade

review.reviewBody: this was fabulous. I did it it in the crock pot and the meat was like butter!! delicious!!

With only 6 hours to marinade before dinner, I left it out for the first hour of marinading, placed it in the refrigerator for 4 hrs. more, and finally took it out an hour prior to grilling. The meat was perfectly tender and very flavorful with just 6 hours in the marinade! 
My lower-carb meal option was to place this atop of a bowl of mixed greens, diced tomatoes, and a bit of guacamole, and dress it with a couple tablespoons of the reserved marinade. It was delicious and filling! 
Unlike some of the other reviewers, I didn't find the citrus flavors overpowering at all. The only modification I made was increasing the quantity of chopped, canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce (I hate to waste an entire can), using 1/4 cup of the peppers and sauce, well chopped. 
Made a great meal - the kids loved it with yellow rice and black beans on the side - and is delicious enough to serve when entertaining.

If there were more stars, I'd give this recipe more. I followed the recipe exact. The video for this showed the meat being grilled but I didn't feel like grilling tonight so I did the cast iron skillet. Oh, I used rump roast as the store didn't have flank steak. The meat marinated for about 12 hours before cooking. I cooked each slice (4 of them) to a medium rare. I sliced each slice cross grain and as the meat had cooled, the reserved marinade was poured into the skillet alone and cooked until it reduced and became fairly thick. Then I returned the thin slices and cooked for only 2 minutes. It was so good, we didn't even use tortillas. I served with fried potatoes and Spanish rice. My boys even made the comment that this was one of the best meals they've had in a long time even though we always eat really good food. I will definitely make this many more times.

I omitted paprika and added a tsp or so more of chipotle, used flank steak and sirloin. I can’t compare it to the original but it was worthy of our lineup!! I’ve served it as a taco filler 2x and on top of romaine with a lime cilantro vinaigrette and cojita cheese. The compliments keep on coming and the whole family loves it! Recently I added sautéed peppers for a fajita style and poured the remaining sauce over it all- absolutely the best carne asada recipe I’ve found. Looking forward to every taco Tuesday ??

My family absolutely loves this recipe!!!! The longer it marinades the better. We added less soy sauce and added more chipotle pepper. We also substituted the flank steak with pork shoulder (about 4lbs) and cooked it for about 4 hrs on 275 degrees. We made this for a Cinco de Mayo party and everyone couldn't get enough! It was amazing!!!

This is a great recipe for anemic people. Vitamin c helps with the absorption of iron in the red meat. However, I did substitute the soy for coconut aminos because soy inhibits iron absorption and is not good for anemia. Everything turned out great and delicious definitely a crowd pleaser. Even my husband loved it with the change of soy for coconut aminos.

I've used this recipe to make carne asada maybe 6-8 times now, and every time I have knocked it out of the park. This most recent time I swapped out soy sauce with liquid shio koji, and it was an absolute GAME CHANGER. If you're feeling adventurous at all, please look into substituting liquid shio koji for soy sauce, and thank the universe later.

Made this today following the marinade directions with the exception that I used a little dried chipotle chiles instead of the teaspoon of canned ones. Weather wasn't good for grilling outside, so I put the meat and the marinade into my slow cooker on high for 3 hours. It was amazing. We decided to serve it "burrito bowl" style like Chipotle Grill, so I put out separate bowls of black beans, rice, home made guacamole & pico de gallo, chopped romaine, shredded mild cheese and low fat sour cream to serve with the beef. Also had whole grain tortillas available for my daughter. Everyone loved this recipe. The meat is very flavorful and tender. Thanks for the recipe and we will be making this again, next time on the grill.

Hands-down, the best marinade I've ever made or had! Used it on lamb chops too, and despite my love of lamb-with-mint-jelly, these chops were the best lamb I've ever eaten! My wife has a garlic sensitivity, so I omitted that. Also, we're not lovers of cilantro, so I subbed in parsley instead... still great!
Everyone really enjoyed this. I marinated for 6 hours and there was tons of flavor. I skipped the chipotle. Also marinated tofu, mushrooms and zucchini.

So I bought a 5# package of chuck cut for carne asada from Costco so I skipped the tenderizing & forking. I also didn't reserve the cup of marinade. It came out better that the prepared raw meat from my butcher that was my favorite. This recipe is fantastic!
Great
at least twice a month. In my opinion the best Mexican Dish I've ever tasted
No changes, it was so flavorful, it was suppose to be for two meals, no leftovers. Our go to recipe now. We served tacos with grilled onions, tomatoes, jalapeños and cilantro on the side.
Soy sauce ruins the marinade. It overpowered all the other flavors. Awful.

I tried this on the steak I had on hand- NY strip- it was so good. I did marinade for 24 hours, no issues. Using it again on 2 tri-tips, I cannot wait to taste. These will be frozen in the marinade, then thawed and grilled. Will update if there's any texture issues

This was great. No changes to the ingredients. I did wait to add the oil to the marinade til after a few hours, so that the water soluble goodies could get sucked up without any interference. Then, all the fat soluble goodies in the herbs and spices had their turn.
Having grown up in San Diego, authentic mexican food was plentiful. This is the closest I’ve ever found.
This was top notch! My husband said this is on your same ole same ole recipes for dinner. I didn’t change a thing!
Absolutely bomb. I changed it to 1/2 a cup of like juice cuz I can’t read, and added 3 culantro leaves. Solid 10/10
